newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl rules out early election in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Kohl rules out early election in Germany.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday rejected opposition calls for early polls in Germany and said the next general election would take place as planned on September 27, 1998.

"We will wait to the evening of that day in September to hear what the voters say," he said in a heated parliamentary debate about his government's attempt to revalue Bundesbank gold to plug gaps in its 1997 budget and qualify for the European single currency.
Leaders of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens urged Kohl in their speeches to sack Finance Minister Theo Waigel and call new elections.
The opposition parties have brought in a resolution on sacking Waigel which the parliament was due to vote on later in the day. Kohl's centre-right majority was expected to vote the motion down.

SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that his party would not consider a grand coalition with Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) if the current government collapsed over a tax dispute with its small liberal Free Democratic Party (FDP) partner.
Waigel has refused to rule out possible tax hikes to finance his 1997 budget but the pro-business FDP has vehemently opposed this.
